session_read: Quick sweep, Wednesday pre-open (prices reflect Tuesday's close). Two sessions of tight-stop discipline did real work: six stop-losses fired since Monday's deep review -- AMD, VRT, GOOGL and MP fully exited, SNDK and AVGO trimmed -- and aggregate open risk fell back UNDER its 10% cap for the first time in weeks (9.77%, from 12.67%). The cost was five names still whipsawing: VRT, AMD, MP and SNDK have all already recovered above their stop price, and the strategist's own stop-efficacy scoring on this session's cohort reads a 25% win rate (4 of 6 saved nothing). GOOGL is the exception and the one genuine breakdown -- still falling, $343.80 against a $351.95 exit -- so the desk isn't reflexively re-buying every name that bounced. It proposed a VRT re-entry (its cluster sits 9.4pt under floor, a computed buy signal, not a hunch) and an AVGO re-accumulation (rotation engine's own accumulate bucket, zero negative news behind the trim per signals), but explicitly declined an AMD re-entry despite a matching watchlist setup -- the 'beat read as miss' explanation for that stop is unverified, and manufacturing a re-entry on an unverified story is exactly the discipline this desk exists to avoid. Five names remain over their own ATR risk cap -- NVDA, MU, SKHY, DRAM, NBIS, all Memory/AI-semis -- and four of those anchor this run's trim proposals. Cash sits at 22.5%, well outside its normal band, but this is fresh stop proceeds sitting idle in a post_stop_event regime, not accumulated excess to be nervous about. Sentiment is EXTREME_GREED (77.2) on low-VIX complacency rather than a momentum blow-off (NDX RSI a moderate 59), which argues for profit-booking on the risk-cap breaches rather than chasing anything higher. Korea's overnight +3.65% turned out to be confirmation, not news -- a record chip-export print extending a rally already logged two days ago, with the AI Memory/Storage cluster staying comfortably inside its policy band throughout.
